5459293589756666022:
Recently, many villagers fell ill after descending the well, her father among them. She has gone days without eating or drinking, growing haggard and thin. Though I am anxious, I don't know how to help for now. 
... 
She adores those singing birds. Maybe I should catch one for her, perhaps it will ease the worry on her brow. 
... 
I thought catching a bird would be easier than digging a well, but I almost had my arm pecked by an eagle that suddenly appeared. When I gave her the bird back in the village, she was truly delighted, constantly asking where I'd gotten it. I didn't know how to explain, so I lied and said I'd caught it by chance... 
... 
Her father's illness worsened. I heard a merchant caravan had medicine that could cure him, but their family had no valuable belongings to trade. The caravan leader, however, was quite interested in the bird I'd caught, willing to exchange medicine for this rare item. When she looked at me, I immediately agreed repeatedly. This bird was always meant for her, how could I refuse? 
... 
When the caravan left, her eyes were red from crying. She stood at the village entrance, staring into the distance until the traces of the carriages and horses vanished in the wind and sand. I knew she couldn't bear to part with the bird. Unable to find words of comfort, I made a vow: though she no longer had the bird's company, I would stay by her side forever and never abandon her.
